facts.raw_span: a right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
recently associated with skin ulceration
the mass had gradually enlarged, was hard in texture, non-tender, and mobile
a 3-cm area of skin breakdown with mild exudation and bleeding over the lesion
a 4.5 × 5.5 cm irregular, poorly defined, hard mass was palpable at the 1 o’clock position in the right breast
overlying ulceration and slight serosanguinous discharge
the lesion was fairly mobile without palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
the left breast was normal
Breast ultrasound and MRI both classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
Chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
Serum breast tumor markers were within normal limits

concepts.why: The patient presents with a hard, non-tender, and mobile breast mass with overlying skin ulceration, which is highly suggestive of invasive ductal carcinoma, as supported by BI-RADS category V classification and chest CT findings.

The patient's presentation of skin breakdown, exudation, and bleeding over the lesion, along with the breast mass, is consistent with inflammatory breast cancer, which is a rare and aggressive subtype of breast cancer.
The patient's breast mass and BI-RADS category V classification may also be consistent with ductal carcinoma in situ, which is a non-invasive form of breast cancer.
The patient's presentation of a hard, mobile, and irregular breast mass may also be consistent with a phyllodes tumor, which is a rare type of breast tumor.
The patient's presentation of a hard and mobile breast mass, along with a normal contralateral breast, may also be consistent with fat necrosis, which is a benign condition.
The patient's presentation of skin breakdown, exudation, and bleeding over the lesion may also be consistent with mastitis, which is an inflammatory condition of the breast.
The patient's presentation of skin breakdown, exudation, and bleeding over the lesion may also be consistent with a breast abscess, which is a localized collection of pus in the breast tissue.
The patient's breast mass and BI-RADS category V classification may also be consistent with lobular carcinoma in situ, which is a non-invasive form of breast cancer.

rationales.F09: BI-RADS category V is highly suggestive of malignancy, which rules out benign conditions like Ductal Carcinoma In Situ, Fat Necrosis, Mastitis, and Breast Abscess.
rationales.F10: Chest CT demonstrating a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy rules out benign conditions like Ductal Carcinoma In Situ, Fat Necrosis, Mastitis, and Breast Abscess.
